ml-lifecycle.prompt: Order the lifecycle from business goal to production monitoring.
ml-lifecycle.steps[0].label: Business Goal Identification
ml-lifecycle.steps[0].detail: Everything downstream inherits this. Without a business goal there is no way to say whether the model is any good.
ml-lifecycle.steps[1].label: ML Problem Framing
ml-lifecycle.steps[1].detail: Translate the goal into a learnable task: what is predicted, from what, and what counts as success.
ml-lifecycle.steps[2].label: Data Collection
ml-lifecycle.steps[2].detail: Assemble the raw material, and establish its provenance and permitted use before it is relied on.
ml-lifecycle.steps[3].label: Data Preprocessing
ml-lifecycle.steps[3].detail: Clean, join, de-duplicate and handle missing values, so the model learns signal rather than artefacts.
ml-lifecycle.steps[4].label: Feature Engineering
ml-lifecycle.steps[4].detail: Shape inputs into representations the algorithm can use. Often the largest single lever on accuracy.
ml-lifecycle.steps[5].label: Model Training
ml-lifecycle.steps[5].detail: Fit parameters on the training split. Cheap to repeat, so it comes after the expensive data work, not before.
ml-lifecycle.steps[6].label: Hyperparameter Tuning
ml-lifecycle.steps[6].detail: Search the settings the model cannot learn for itself, evaluated on validation data rather than test.
ml-lifecycle.steps[7].label: Model Evaluation
ml-lifecycle.steps[7].detail: Measure against held-out data and the business metric. This is the gate, not a formality.
ml-lifecycle.steps[8].label: Model Deployment (Inference and Prediction)
ml-lifecycle.steps[8].detail: Serve predictions for real requests, with the same preprocessing as training or the results will not match.
ml-lifecycle.steps[9].label: Model Monitoring
ml-lifecycle.steps[9].detail: Watch inputs, outputs and quality in production. This is where drift surfaces, and it never ends.
